In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the prefrontal cortex (PFC) in the cognitive control of action.
how the prefrontal cortex (PFC) contributes to cognitive processes.
the neural mechanisms of cognitive control and the role of prefrontal cortex in these mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PFdl is involved in the encoding of strategies and responses, while PFo and PFp are involved in the encoding and monitoring of responses and the encoding of strategies, respectively.
PFdl, PFo, and PFp each have unique functions that are not shared with the other prefrontal areas.

PFdl is involved in the selection and implementation of strategies and responses, PFo in the assignment of outcomes to strategies and responses, and PFp in the assignment of cognitive outcomes to cognitive processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PFdl is involved in strategy generation, and that PFo and PFp are involved in outcome assignment.
PFdl encodes strategies and responses, and PFo encodes strategies and rewards.
the dorsolateral, orbital, and polar prefrontal cortex are all involved in the cognitive processes of strategy selection and response generation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
different prefrontal regions encode different types of information, and that these different types of information are used to perform different cognitive processes.
the three prefrontal areas encode different aspects of the task, and that the information encoded by these areas is not the same across tasks.
the three prefrontal areas are specialized for different aspects of cognition, and the same cognitive process can be supported by different areas depending on task demands.
